(By Sri.S.Maheswara, Advocate)
 *******
 JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against respondents seeking compensation on account of death of one Sri.Praveen Kumar @ Prabin Kumar S/o Kusheshwarprasad Mahto, who died in Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
On 26-04-2022 at about 05.30 p.m, the said Praveen Kumar @ Prabin Kumar was proceeding in his Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-41-EE-3919 from Mahadevapura to Nelamangala to go to his house and when he reached near Mahadevapura Cadbury Chocolote Factory, Nelamangala Kunigal NH-75, at that time a Crane bearing No.KA-52-N-3441 driven by (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.3669/2022 its driver, came from back side at very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed Motor Cycle and crane ran over the rider Praveen Kumar @ Prabin Kumar.

sentences.text: Due to death of the deceased, the petitioners are facing great hardship and irreparable loss and mental agony which cannot be compensated by any means and suffering from untold mental agony, financial loss.
The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending Crane by its driver and in this regard the Madanayakanahalli Police have registered a case against driver of offending Crane.

The respondent No.1 being the RC owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending Crane, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- to the petitioners with cost and interest at the rate of 18% p.a.
03.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent, hence, was placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.3669/2022 objections.
During pendency of the petition, petitioner No.4 reported to be dead.
Hence, petitioner No.4 is deleted from the cause title.

04. The respondent No.2 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioners and admits that this respondent is the insurer of Crane bearing No.KA-52-N-3441 and liability to indemnify the respondent No.1 is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and contended that the offending Crane is not involved in the accident and the deceased was not wearing helmet as on the date of accident and the driver of the Crane was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and further was not qualified for holding or obtaining such driving licence, thereby,
the owner of the vehicle committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy and the Charge sheet is filed U/Sec 3(1) r/w Sec.181 of IMV Act and also denied manner of accident, age,
occupation, income of deceased and dependency of the petitioners with the deceased, cause of death and expenses incurred by the petitioners.
The compensation claimed is exorbitant and hence, pray for dismiss the petition against respondent No.2 with costs.

On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, the following Issues has been framed by my learned predecessor:-
ISSUES 01.
Whether petitioners prove that they are the LRs/dependents of deceased Sri.Praveen Kumar S/o Kusheshwar Prasad Mahto?

02. Whether petitioners prove that deceased Sri.Praveen Kumar was died in RTA arising out of the accident alleged to have been taken place on 26.04.2022 at about 5.30 p.m, near Mahadevapura Cadbury Chocolate Factory, Nelamangala-Kunigal NH- 75 Road, Bengaluru Rural District, due to rash and negligence driving of Crane by the driver bearing registration No. KA-52-N-3441 as alleged in the petition?

If so, what amount & whom?

06. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 is examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to 17 and closed their side evidence.

07. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.2 got examined Driver of Crane and its Legal Officer as RW.1 (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.3669/2022 and 2 and got marked 4 documents as Ex.R.1 to 4 and closed its side evidence.
08.
Heard both sides.

The counsel for respondent No.2 has filed written arguments and has relied upon the citation reported in SLP (Civil) No.11757/2025 in the case of Mahaveer V/s The Branch Manager, United India Insurance Co. Ltd., and others.

My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.3669/2022  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- Petitioner No.1 in her affidavit stated that, she is the wife, petitioners No.2 and 3 are the sons and petitioner No.5 is the mother of the deceased.
To prove the said facts, she has produced notarized copies of Aadhaar cards of deceased and other petitioners and Driving licence of the deceased as per Ex.P.12 to 17.
There is no dispute regarding dependency of the petitioners with the deceased.

These documents clearly goes to show that, the petitioners are the legal heirs and Malathi Devi vs Nagaraju .L on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187169413/
4 dependents on the deceased.
Hence, I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:- The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 got herself examined as PW.1 and in her chief-examination evidence she has reiterated the petition averments therein.

Though, she has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioners that due to rash and negligent driving of the offending Crane by (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.3669/2022 its driver, deceased sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident and died on the spot.
On perusal of exhibited documents, Ex.P.1 FIR registered at Nelamangala Traffic Police against driver of offending Crane.
Ex.P.2 is the Complaint shows that due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending Crane the accident took place, in which the deceased sustained injuries and died.

Ex.P.3, 4 and 7 are Spot Mahazar, Sketch and Seizer Mahazar showing the place of accident on NH-75 Nelamangala-Kunigal Road, opposite to Cadburys Chocolate Factory, Mahadevapura, Kasaba Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk and after investigation the Police have seized the said offending vehicle, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.5 is copy of Notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act issued to the owner of the offending Crane.

Ex.P.6 is copy of Reply to notice which discloses that the owner of the offending Crane has stated that one Mohammad Samim Akthar S/o Sonai was driving the offending vehicle and had no driving licence at the time of accident and said vehicle had valid insurance as on the date of accident.
Ex.P.8 is copy of IMV report which discloses that both vehicles are involved in the accident and Motor Cycle of the deceased got damaged.
Ex.P.9 is Inquest report of deceased Praveen Kumar.

Ex.P.10 is PM report of (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.3669/2022 deceased Praveen Kumar shows death is due to sudden cardio respiratory arrest secondary to multiple grievous injuries to the vital organs of the body like right kidney intestines etc., due to RTA.

Ex.P.11 is Charge sheet shows after investigation the Investigation Officer has filed Charge sheet against driver of the offending Crane for the offences punishable U/Sec 279, 304(A) of IPC and Sec.181 and 187 of IMV Act for the reasons that the driver of the offending Crane after causing accident left the vehicle and fled away from the accident spot and he did not possess driving licence at the time of accident.

The oral and documentary evidence clearly goes to show that the accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending Crane and deceased sustained injuries and died on the spot.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.3:-
This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Praveen Kumar @ Prabin Kumar, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

The PW.1/petitioner No.1 in her evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 44 years (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.3669/2022 and was working as Granite Mestri as own work and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m and has spent Rs.50,000/-
towards funeral expenses.
Due to death of the deceased, the petitioners are facing great hardship and irreparable loss, mental agony and financial loss.
13. It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age of the deceased.
The petitioners have not produced any birth certificate, school records and SSLC marks card of the deceased to show his exact date of birth.
However, they have produced Ex.P.12 Aadhaar card and Ex.P.16 Driving licence of deceased.

The alleged accident occurred on 26.04.2022 and hence it appears that as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased is 44 years.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased as 44 years as on the date of accident.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 41 to 45 is "14".

sentences.text: In the case on hand, undoubtedly the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioners No.2 and 3 are the children and petitioners No.5 is the mother of the deceased and they are dependents on the income of the deceased.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.

Since deceased was aged about 44 years at the time of accident and was self employee and he comes in the age group of 40 to 50 years, 25% income should be added to the monthly income towards future prospects which would be (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.3669/2022 result in the income to be (15,500 +
3,875) = Rs.19,375/-.

Since there are four dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th of the income of the deceased towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (19,375 - 4,844) = Rs.14,531/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.14,531/-.
As the deceased was aged about 44 years, the multiplier of 14 would have to be applied.
Consequently the claimants would be entitled for a sum of Rs.24,41,208/- (Rs.14,531 x 12 x 14) towards loss of dependency.

16. In view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & Others case, in respect to loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.

Therefore, petitioner No.1 and 5 are entitled for Rs.48,400/- each towards loss (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.3669/2022 of spousal and filial consortium.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.26,54,308/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
19.

Regarding liability:- To disprove the case of the petitioners, the respondent No.2 got examined Driver of the offending vehicle as RW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has stated that as he was going forward, the biker in front of him crashed into his crane.
At the time of the accident, he was driving a tractor.
He have permission to drive a tractor and LMV as per Ex.R.1.
Since he don't have a driving licence to drive the car, the final report showed that he don't have a driving license.

During the course of cross-examination by the petitioners' counsel he admits that as on the date of accident he was driving (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.3669/2022 the crane and on the day of the accident,
the crane ran over the body of the deceased, causing a terrible accident.

When he saw it, he got scared and ran away, thinking that the public would beat him up and admits that he had a driving license to drive Crane No. KA-52-N-3441 on the date of accident and he has produced Ex.R.1 copy of driving licence and Ex.R.2 Vehicle history report, which shows that driver was authorized to drive Tractor, LMV-NT only.

20. Further, the respondent No.2 got examined its Legal Officer as RW.2 and in his chief-examination evidence he has stated that the Charge sheet filed U/Sec 3(1) r/w Sec.181 of M.V.
Act for not holding valid and effective driving licence by the driver to drive the vehicle as on the date Malathi Devi vs Nagaraju .L on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187169413/
7 of accident and as per Ex.R.2 the laden weight of the vehicle is 9,800 kgs and it is more than the weight of 7,500 kgs.
As such the owner of the vehicle has violated the terms and conditions of the policy and hence, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

During his cross-examination he admits that as per Investigation Officer report the accident occurred due to negligence of Crane vehicle driver and all documents of the said vehicle is correct, but driving licence is not valid and Police have filed Charge sheet against driver (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.3669/2022 of offending crane and he has produced Policy at Ex.R.4 which shows that as on the date of accident the policy of the offending Crane is valid and is in force.
21. On perusal of Ex.R.2 the unladen weight of the offending crane is 9,800 kgs, which is come in the category of transport vehicle.
But the driver of offending vehicle had driving licence of LMV-NT only, hence the owner of the offending vehicle has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
In Ex.P.11 Charge Sheet the Investigation Officer has submitted Charge sheet against driver of the offending Crane for driving the Crane without driving licence as on the date of accident.

Therefore,
in view of the facts and circumstances of the case and in view of ratio laid down in the above said citations relied by counsels for petitioners and respondent No.2 in view of recent Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Akula Narayana V/s The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and another, in Civil Appeal No.013509/2025 (Arising out of SLP (C) No.8434/2023 dt:10.11.2025, has upheld the principle of pay and recovery and has clearly held that, "Where the contract of insurance is not disputed, even on breach of insurance conditions, this Court had allowed recovery of compensation from the insurer by giving right to the (SCCH-3) 18 M.V.C.No.3669/2022 insurer to recover the same from the vehicle owner.

entities.text: Akula Narayana V/s The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The pay and recovery principle has been consistently followed even though it was doubted in a reference which remained unanswered".
22.

Therefore, this tribunal is the opinion that, since policy of the offending Crane is valid and is in force as on the date of accident, since driver of the offending Crane drove the same without driving licence, it is a fundamental breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, respondent No.2 Insurance Company shall pay compensation amount to the petitioners with a liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending Crane.
Accordingly, Issue No.3 is answered partly in the affirmative.

23. Issue No.4:- In view of reasons assigned to Issues No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 are partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.26,54,308/- (Rupees Twenty six lakhs fifty four thousand three hundred and eight only) with (SCCH-3) 19 M.V.C.No.3669/2022 interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amounts with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment, with a liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending Crane.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Due to death of the deceased, the petitioners are facing great hardship and irreparable loss, mental agony and financial loss.
13. It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age of the deceased.
The petitioners have not produced any birth certificate, school records and SSLC marks card of the deceased to show his exact date of birth.
However, they have produced Ex.P.12 Aadhaar card and Ex.P.16 Driving licence of deceased.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased as 44 years as on the date of accident.
In order to prove the avocation and income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents.
In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.
During his cross-examination he admits that as per Investigation Officer report the accident occurred due to negligence of Crane vehicle driver and all documents of the said vehicle is correct, but driving licence is not valid and Police have filed Charge sheet against driver (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.3669/2022 of offending crane and he has produced Policy at Ex.R.4 which shows that as on the date of accident the policy of the offending Crane is valid and is in force.
But the driver of offending vehicle had driving licence of LMV-NT only, hence the owner of the offending vehicle has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
In Ex.P.11 Charge Sheet the Investigation Officer has submitted Charge sheet against driver of the offending Crane for driving the Crane without driving licence as on the date of accident.
Therefore, this tribunal is the opinion that, since policy of the offending Crane is valid and is in force as on the date of accident, since driver of the offending Crane drove the same without driving licence, it is a fundamental breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
